facts.text: Overtown, once called Colored Town, became Miami’s historic black commercial hub during the Jim Crow era.
The Lyric Theater, built in 1913, was the “Little Broadway” of Overtown, hosting legends like Ella Fitzgerald and Louis Armstrong.
Overtown’s streets were once barred from black residents by the 1964 Civil Rights Act, forcing them to use passes to enter nearby white neighborhoods.
The neighborhood’s community garden, founded by Marvin Dunn, turned an overgrown lot into a thriving green space for residents and volunteers.
Agnes Episcopal Church, founded by Bahamian immigrants, remains a musical sanctuary that unites Overtown’s diverse faith community.
Overtown’s historic heart includes the Dorsey Memorial Library, the first city‑owned building built specifically as a library in 1941.
